sentences.text: The present appeal emanates from the judgment and award dated 11.04.2017 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.) and 4 th Ad-hoc District Judge, Kheda at Nadiad in MACP No.790 and 791 of 2009.

2. The captioned First Appeal No.1191 of 2018 has been filed in MACP No.790/2009 by Dindayal Babulal Shahni (Pillion Rider), and First Appeal No.1129 of 2018 has been filed in MACP no.791/2009 (Motorcycle Driver).

C/FA/1191/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023  
3.

By the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.47,250/- in MACP No.790/2009 and Rs.96,265/- in MACP No.791/ 2009.
4.

The brief facts of the case are as under:-
4.1

It is the case of the applicants that the accident was occurred on 29.04.2009, at about 9:30 a.m., on Balej-Umreth Road, Near Untkhari Patia, when the applicant of MACP No.790/2009 was coming from Khankuva to Pansora by sitting on Motorcycle No.GJ-07-AH-5841 as pillion rider and the said motorcycle was being driven by applicant of MACP No.791/2009 and when they reached on the spot of accident at that time opponent No.2 was came by driving Hyundai Car bearing No.GJ-07-AG-6388 with full speed and in negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle from back side and the accident was taken place.

Due to the said accident,
the appellants have sustained the injuries as mentioned in their medical certificates.
SUBMISSIONS 5.
Learned advocate Mr.Darji appearing for the appellants has assailed the judgment and award Dindayal Babulal Shahni vs Gayatriben Shivshankar Joshi on 19 January, 2023

2 passed by the Tribunal on three grounds:-(1) with regard to determine of negligence of the appellant(MACP no.791/2009) , who was the driver of the motorcycle having registration number being GJ-7-AH-5841 with regard to the determination of negligence to the extent of 35%, (2) with regard to the determination of the income of the appellants of at Rs.3,400/- and (3) with regard to the determination of the disability and the denial of prospective income.
NEUT  C/FA/1191/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023  unde 6.

Learned advocate Mr.Darji, while referring to the findings of fixing the liability of the appellant-Driver to the extent of 35%, has submitted that the finding is premised only on the cross-examination of the appellant and the pillion rider i.e. (appellant of First Appeal No.1191 of 2018 in MACP Case No.790 of 2009).

He has submitted that in fact the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. the Hyundai Car having registration No.GJ-7-AG-6388 did not entered into the witness box hence, in absence of any evidence of the driver of the Hyundai Car, the liability of the appellant could not have been fixed and negligence of the appellant could not have been determined to the extent of 35% and that of the driver of the Hyundai Car at 65%.
7.

Learned advocate Mr.Darji has also submitted that in fact a charge- sheet was also filed against the driver of the Hyundai Car (at Exh.36), however, only because the appellant-driver and his pillion rider have in their cross-examinations described the accident the liability is fixed to the extent of 35%.

It is further submitted that the insurance company has not led any evidence with regard to negligence and hence, the Tribunal ought not to have held the driver of the motorcycle negligent and in the present case the driver of the Hyundai Car is required to be held 100% negligent for the accident.

It is submitted that in fact the evidence reveals that the appellant was travelling on a motorcycle through a narrow road and was entering on the main road and since the car was being driven in a rash and negligent manner; the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Hyundai Car and hence, the appellant cannot be held liable to the extent of 35% for the accident.

In support of his submissions, he has placed reliance on the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1191/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined dated 26.10.2021 passed in First Appeal No.1339 of 2020.

Reliance is also placed by him on the judgments of the Supreme Court in the case of Khenyei vs. New India Assurance Company Dindayal Babulal Shahni vs Gayatriben Shivshankar Joshi on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91680143/

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that the judgment and award to that extent is required to be set aside.

8. So far as the fixation of income is concerned, learned advocate Mr.Darji has submitted that the same is also fixed at lower side by the Tribunal by assessing the income of the appellants at Rs.3,400/-.

He has submitted that in fact both the appellants are/were working as Commission Agents in vegetables business and the affidavit of the witnesses recorded below Exhibits 44, 46 and 48 would prove that they were earning an amount of Rs.10,000/- per month, however, the Tribunal has not fixed the income by appreciating the oral evidence and the same is also required to be enhanced.
8.1. Learned advocate Mr.Darji has further submitted that the Tribunal has also fallen in error in assessing the disabilities of both the appellants.
He has submitted that the Tribunal has fixed the disability of the appellant-pillion Rider at 10% body as a whole, which is contrary to the evidence on record.
It is submitted that as per the disability certificate vide Exh.41 issued by one Dr.Yogesh Parikh, the appellant sustained permanent disability of 30% body as a whole.

It is submitted that the appellant-Pillion Rider has suffered the permanent disability of 16% in right lower limb and 14% in right upper limb and even if the oral evidence of the doctor as well as the certificate, which is produced at Exh.41 is concerned, the total disability of the limb is assessed at 30% by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1191/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined

the Tribunal itself,
however, while assessing the disability of the entire body, the same is reduced to 10% and it should be 15% as a body as a whole instead of 10%.
So far the Motorcycle-Driver (MACP No.791/2009) it is submitted that in his case also the physical disability is also incorrectly assesed.

Reliance is placed by him at the Medical Certificate, Exh.42, wherein it is opined that the Motorcycle driver has sustained 22% disability body as a whole, however, the Tribunal has determined the same as 15%
which is erroneous and contrary to the record.
Thus, it is submitted that the disability is accordingly required to be re-assessed.
8.2. It is further submitted that the appellants are also entitled to loss of prospective income.

Thus,
it is submitted that the impugned award of the Tribunal is required to be modified by enhancing the necessary compensation.

8.3. While referring to the judgment in the case of Khenyei (supra), learned advocate Mr.Darji has submitted that so far as the inter se liability of joint tortfeasor is concerned, the respondent-insurance company has to file appropriate suit or proceedings to recover the said amount.

It is submitted that the insurance company has to recover the amount from the joint tortfeasors i.e. the driver of the motorcycle i.e. the appellant of MACP No.791 of 209 and a separate proceedings in the form of suit is required to be filed by the insurance company in order to recover the amount.
9.

In response to the aforesaid submissions, learned advocate Mr.Dholakia has submitted that so far as there cannot be any cavil on proposition of law with regard to the fixation of negligency, as enunciated NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1191/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined in Dindayal Babulal Shahni vs Gayatriben Shivshankar Joshi on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91680143/
4 the judgments, which are cited by the learned advocate Mr.Darji appearing for the appellants.

It is,
however, submitted that in the present case, the law enunciated by the Apex Court in said decisions will not apply looking to the admissions of the appellants.

It is submitted by him that in fact the pillion rider i.e. (the appellant of First Appeal No.1191 of 2018) has deposed in his cross-examination, and it is elicited that the motorcycle was being driven from the narrow road and they were entering on the main road and at that relevant time, the accident has occurred with the Hyundai Car, which was travelling on the main road.
It is thus submitted that in fact the appellant was also equally liable for the accident as he should have first ascertained the traffic on the main road before entering on it.

Learned advocate Mr.Dholakia has submitted that in fact in wake of the aforesaid admission in the cross-examination, there is no further need for the insurance company to lead evidence in this regard.
It is also submitted that in fact the Tribunal was generous enough to hold the Motorcycle driver negligent to the extent of 35%, which was in fact required to be enhanced.

9.1. It is further submitted that merely because charge-sheet has been filed against the driver of the Hyundai Car, the same would not ipso facto be considered as an evidence for setting aside or reducing the negligency in the accident on the part of the appellant.
It is submitted that until and unless the offence, for which the Car Driver is charge-sheeted, is established, no reliance can be placed on the contents of such charge- sheet.

10. Learned advocate Mr.Dholakia has submitted that even the panchnama, Exh.35 also reveals that the accident has occurred when the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1191/2018 JUDGMENT DATED:
19/01/2023 undefined motorcycle, which was driven by the appellant all of a sudden was driven to the main road from the narrow road and hence, the Tribunal has precisely determined the negligency of the driver of the motorcycle to the extent of 35%.

With regard to fixation of income by the Tribunal at the rate of Rs.3,400 of the appellant, learned advocate Mr.Dholakia has submitted that the same does not require any interference as it is an established fact that no documentary evidence was produced in the form of either salary, income tax returns, etc. to establish that the appellants were earning an amount of Rs.10,000/- per month being a Commission Agent in selling the vegetables.
Thus, it is submitted that the income, which is assessed by the Tribunal, does not require any interference.
So far as the assessment of disability is concerned, learned advocate Mr.Dholakia has also submitted that the same is appropriately passed and does not require any further modification.

10.1. While placing reliance on the observations made by the Supreme Court in the case of Khenyei (supra), learned advocate Mr.Dholakia has placed reliance on the observations made in the paragraph no.17 and has submitted that the insurance company is not required to file separate proceedings and the claim can be assessed in the execution proceedings, which would be filed by the claimant.
Thus, it is submitted that the insurance company is not required to file separate proceedings or suit against the joint tortfeasor i.e. the driver of the motorcycle.

11. In response to the submission of the prospective income, learned advocate Mr.Darji has submitted that in fact the evidence of the appellant as well as the pillion rider reveal that there is no loss of income caused to them in view of the accident or the disability, and hence, the same is also Dindayal Babulal Shahni vs Gayatriben Shivshankar Joshi on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91680143/

CONCLUSION 12.

The submissions advanced by the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties establish that the appellants have confined the determination of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the aforenoted factors.

The appellant is challenging the findings of the Tribunal holding the appellant-Motorcycle driver (First Appeal No.1129/18-MACP No.791/2009) to the extent of 35%
negligent and the driver of the car to the extent of 65% negligent for the accident.
13. The submissions of the Motorcycle driver is primarily premised on the fact that the driver of the Hyundai Car has not entered into the witness box and he is also charge-sheeted in the criminal proceedings.
The second submission, which is advanced before this Court, is that the insurance company has not led the evidence establishing that the appellant was 35% negligent for the accident in question.

The Tribunal, after assessing the documentary as well as the oral evidence, has determined the negligency on the part of the respective drivers to the extent of 65% and 35% i.e. the driver of the Hyundai Car and the present appellant, who was driving the motorcycle, respectively,
on the basis of the statement elicited in the cross-examination of both the appellants, driver and the pillion rider i.e. the appellant of First Appeal No.1191 of 2018 (claimant of MACP No.790 of 2009).

14. This Court has perused the cross-examination of the pillion-rider (Dindayal Babulal Sahani)
recorded below Exh.30.

A categorical statement has been elicited from his cross-examination is as below:-
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1191/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined "The accident occurred at cross road.
At that time we were supposed to go Pansora to Khankuva and the said car came from our right side...
... It is true that, out motorcycle was coming to main road from the narrow road.
When our motorcycle all of a sudden climbed from the narrow road to wide road, the accident occurred.

The appellant i.e. the Motorcyle Driver (First Appeal No.1129 of 2018) Rajesh Ramaneresh Yadav) was examined below Exh.31 and his cross-examination is elicited thus:-
"It is true that it was a narrow road, on which I was driving motorcycle.
It is true that the car was on the main road at that time.
It is true that we were going to the main road from the narrow road on motorcycle.
It is true that the accident occurred at cross road.
It is true that the front portion of my motorcycle got dashed with front portion of the car.

It is true that both the vehicles were on well built road when the incident occurred"

sentences.text: Both the appellants are the injured witnesses.
The combined reading of their depositions, which are mentioned hereinabove, would reveal and transpire that the accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of the Motorcycle driver also.

The documentary evidence in the form of panchnama is also perused by this Court, which is below Exh.35, which clearly transpires that both the vehicles have dashed on the main road from the front side and the accident has occurred at the crossroads.

The evidence reveals that that the motorcycle was being driven from NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1191/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined narrow road and while "climbing" and approaching from a narrow road to the main road from which the Hyundai Car was coming, the accident has occurred.
Thus, it was expected from the appellant, who was the driver of the motorcycle, to first ascertain on going traffic before driving and climbing to the main road.

16. In the considered opinion of this Court, this Court does not find any infirmity or illegality in determining that the driver of the Hyundai Car as 65% negligent and the present driver of Motorcycle as 35% negligent.
Hence, the finding in this regard does not require any interference.

17. So far as the quantum of compensation, which is determined after assessing the income of the appellant at Rs.3,500/-, this Court is of the opinion that the oral evidence establishes that the appellants were the Commission Agents in the vegetables business.

In support of their assertion of having monthly income of Rs.10,000/-, no documentary evidence is produced, hence, as per the settled proposition of law, the minimum wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act by the State Government for the skilled and unskilled labourers prevailing at the time of the accident is required to be considered for deriving the income.
It is not disputed that the minimum wages, which have been determined for an unskilled labourer in the State of Gujarat for the period between 01.04.2009 to 30.09.2009, is Rs.3,700/-.
Thus, it can safely be presumed that the appellants would be earning more than Rs.3,500/- when the accident has occurred on 29.04.2009.
Hence, for determining just compensation, the income of each of the appellant is determined at Rs.4000/-.

sentences.text: The next factor, which requires to be considered, is with regard to the determination of the physical disability of the Pillion Rider (First Appeal NO.1191/2018).
The oral evidence of Dr.Yogesh Parikh below Exh.39 as well as the disability certificate below Exh.41, it is revealed that the body as a whole, the Pillion rider has suffered 23% disability.

However, the Tribunal, while examining the disability certificate, has determined the total disability for the limbs as 30% i.e. (16%+14%) and has assessed the disability as a body as a whole in case of the appellant @ 10%, which in the considered opinion of this Court, is required to be determined at 15% looking to the disability of 30% in limbs.
It is well settled proposition of law that the disability as a body as a whole is required to be assessed after looking to the total disability of the limbs.

In the present case, it is not in dispute and as per the evidence on record, the total limb disability is 30% and hence, the Tribunal has fallen in error in determining the disability as a body as a whole @ 10% and hence, the same is required to be determined @ 15% in case of Pillion driver(F.A No.1191/18-MACP no.790/2009).
19. Accordingly, in case of the Driver of the Motorcycle,(F.A No.1129/18-MACP.791/2009), the Tribunal has also fallen in error in determining the same at 15%.
In his case, the evidence reveals that the driver has suffered 22% disability as a whole, however, the Tribunal has assessed the same at 15% which is contrary to the evidence.
Hence, the permanent disability of the motorcycle driver is required to be determined at 22% instead of 15%.

20. So far as the claim of the appellant with regard to the prospective loss of income is concerned, it would be apposite to refer to their NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1191/2018 JUDGMENT DATED:
19/01/2023 undefined depositions.

In the cross-examination, it is elicited from the appellants that in fact there is no loss of income and it has been admitted by them that there is no future loss of income and no decrease in their monthly income even after the occurrence of the accident.
Thus, in view of the categorical statement made by the appellants, the prospective income of the appellant cannot be determined and the compensation in this regard cannot be awarded.

However, in the considered opinion of this Court, looking to the nature of injuries and the period of hospitalization of both the appellants, the amount awarded towards pain, shock and sufferings is required to be enhanced from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.15,000/-.
21.

In view of the aforesaid findings, the compensation is determined as under:-

respective however the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.72,620/- and Rs.1,48,100/- which is required to be deducted from the compensation arrived at by this Court.

Thus, the appellants would be entitled to an additional amount of Rs.36,180/- and Rs.47,320/-, respectively with 6% interest from the date of filing of the claim petitions till the realization of the amount.
Accordingly, the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified to the aforesaid extent.
The additional amount along with the interest shall be deposited before the Tribunal within a period of three months, which shall be disbursed to the claimants after due verification.
23. In view of the above, the First Appeals are partly allowed.
Record and proceedings shall be returned to the concerned Tribunal forthwith.

24. It will be open for the insurance company to file execution proceedings against the joint tortfeasor with regard to filing of execution proceedings by the insurance company or the respective appellants in both the matters.
It will be open for the respective parties to take all the available contentions before the execution court with regard to liability of recovery as well as the disbursement.

In his case, the evidence reveals that the driver has suffered 22% disability as a whole, however, the Tribunal has assessed the same at 15% which is contrary to the evidence.
Hence, the permanent disability of the motorcycle driver is required to be determined at 22% instead of 15%.
